nameplate-capacity.short: The most power a plant is built to deliver, in kilowatts (kW) or megawatts (MW). A 100 MW solar farm makes 100 MW only in full sun.

full-load-hours.short: A year's output expressed as hours at nameplate capacity: capacity factor × 8,760. A solar farm with a capacity factor of 0.17 makes as much as 1,489 hours at full power.

installed-cost.short: Everything it takes to build a power plant and connect it, divided by its nameplate capacity, in US dollars per kilowatt (US$/kW).

operations-and-maintenance.short: The yearly cost of running a plant: staff, repairs, insurance, land lease. Fixed O&M is per kW per year; variable O&M is per MWh produced.

cost-of-capital.short: The yearly return lenders and investors demand for financing a plant, usually a weighted average cost of capital (WACC) of debt and equity. It is the discount rate in an LCOE.

land-use-intensity.short: Land occupied per unit of electricity produced each year, for example square metres per MWh/yr. It can count only the direct footprint or the whole site and the mines that feed it.

co2-equivalent.short: A way to add different greenhouse gases together: each gas is counted as the mass of carbon dioxide that would warm the planet as much over 100 years.

dispatchable.short: A source that can raise or lower its output when the grid operator asks, such as hydro with a reservoir, geothermal, bioenergy or gas. Sun and wind are not, unless paired with storage.
